text: FIELD has a documented, repeated pattern of correct drama-scoring code that is never wired to a real caller -- four confirmed instances, one of them independently re-confirmed dead two months after being written. This is the base rate against which any claim that the weather hook 'fires in production' should be read.
falsifier: re-read that outbox doc; it tabulates the four instances with wired? = No on each
resolutionNote: Doc re-read (jubilant-bassoon:docs/outbox/chat-update-2026-07-30-drama-dead-code-pattern.md). By the falsifier's stated test the claim passes: the Wired? column reads No on all four rows. But re-reading shows the claim's WORDING overcounts. The Coded? column reads No on three of the four -- NFL WPA Drama Profiles, Escalating Milestones and the Soccer 4-layer formula were designed and never built. Only PL Final Day Stakes is 'correct code with zero real callers', and the doc says so itself: 'The PL Final Day case is the sharpest data point: this is not a stale idea, it is correct, tested code sitting completely unreachable'. Its own prose scopes the pattern loosely -- 'sometimes with real external data ... even correct math coded into the client'. So: four confirmed instances of DESIGNED-AND-NEVER-REACHED-PRODUCTION, of which exactly ONE is coded-but-unwired. The base rate this claim was invoked to supply is therefore weaker than stated, and a direct counter-instance exists: weatherDramaModifier, the weather hook in question, IS wired -- 'sitBonus += weatherDramaModifier(wxEntry)' at src/legacy/field.js:22813 and index.html:27697.
